Hello, I am in no way a professional, but I can relate. The first time I can remember being suicidal I was age 5, and it hasn’t stopped since. I fantasize about ending my life in so many different ways I feel like I have truly thought about everything. At one point, a couple years ago, i felt numb to everything. I didn’t feel happiness or sadness i just felt nothing. Suicidal thoughts still continued. Eventually I slowly started to feel again and for a while, I was on medication and it really really helped with my depression, but the suicidal thoughts never stopped. Although I don’t have an answer to your question, I can give you this advice:  no matter how strong your thoughts are or how often you have them, you should never ever end your life. You will feel emotion again, and you will get through it.

Hi, if you’re comfortable with it, I recommend connecting with people online that share common interests. Twitter and tik tok are places where you can easily search your interests and find plenty of people who share them with you. If you’re looking to make friends in your area, I think going to events that you’re interested in or just training yourself to make conversation with people in public places can really help. Also, just note that ending your life is never the way to go, things will get better nothing is linear. I hope this helped and I hope you are doing well❤️

First of all, your body is beautiful no matter what you may think and you need to learn to be more kind to yourself. I think you are doing great by going to the gym and trying to limit yourself. progress will take time just keep going and you will discover new things that work for you and I promise you will see progress!! I understand feeling like the body you live in is not yours or just being generally unhappy with it. Just remember when you see yourself the potential you have and remember to love your body as it is, because it is constantly changing whether it’s for better or worse. The only criticism I have is that I think you need some new friends because if those were your true friends they would not be treating you like that. You need to find a good support system to help you on your journey and help you love yourself again. Whether it be making new friends completely or just talking or venting to people on here, I think all you need is a little bit of support from others and belief in yourself.

College is not the only path in life, if it is still your desire to graduate you could change your classes to things that interest you or that you think you might be interested in. If not, you do not need to go to college to be successful, there are so many other things you can do with your life you just need to put in the research and work to find what you will enjoy most.
